def transform(x):
    n = len(x)
    if n % 2:                     # odd length
        mid = x[n // 2]
        head = x[:n // 2]
        tail = x[n // 2 + 1:]
        return tail[::-1] + [mid] + [mid, mid] + head[::-1]
    else:                         # even length
        left = x[n // 2 - 1]      # element at position n/2 (1‑based)
        right = x[n // 2]         # element at position n/2+1 (1‑based)
        head = x[:n // 2 - 1]     # elements before the two middle ones

        # decide which extra copies to add
        if tail and left > max(tail):
            extras = [left, left]          # duplicate the left middle twice
        else:

        return tail[::-1] + [right, left] + extras + head[::-1]

def transform(x):
    n = len(x)
    if n % 2:                     # odd length
        mid = x[n // 2]
        head = x[:n // 2]
        tail = x[n // 2 + 1:]
        middle = [mid] * 3
    else:                         # even length
        left = x[n // 2 - 1]      # element just left of centre
        right = x[n // 2]         # element just right of centre
        head = x[:n // 2 - 1]     # elements before the two centre ones
        tail = x[n // 2 + 1:]     # elements after the two centre ones

        if n == 4:                # the only even length where both sides have a single element
            # fill the four‑slot middle part with two copies of the outer element,
            # then the right centre, then the left centre
            middle = [head[0], head[0], right, left]
        elif left < right and n % 4 == 0:
            # when the left centre is smaller and the length is a multiple of 4,
            # mirror the two centre values
            middle = [right, left, left, right]
        else:
            # default case: right centre once, left centre three times
            middle = [right, left, left, left]

    return tail[::-1] + middle + head[::-1]

def transform(x):
    n = len(x)
    if n % 2:                     # odd length
        mid = x[n // 2]
        head = x[:n // 2]
        tail = x[n // 2 + 1:]
        middle = [mid] * 3
    else:                         # even length
        left = x[n // 2 - 1]      # element just left of centre
        right = x[n // 2]         # element just right of centre
        head = x[:n // 2 - 1]     # elements before the two centre ones
        tail = x[n // 2 + 1:]     # elements after the two centre ones

        if n == 4:                # the only even length where both sides have a single element
            # fill the four‑slot middle part with two copies of the outer element,
            # then the right centre, then the left centre
            middle = [head[0], head[0], right, left]
        elif left < right and n % 4 == 0:
            # when the left centre is smaller and the length is a multiple of 4,
            # mirror the two centre values
            middle = [right, left, left, right]
        else:
            # default case: right centre once, left centre three times
            middle = [right, left, left, left]

    return tail[::-1] + middle + head[::-1]

def transform(x):
    n = len(x)
    if n % 2:                     # odd length
        mid = x[n // 2]
        head = x[:n // 2]
        tail = x[n // 2 + 1:]
        middle = [mid] * 3
    else:                         # even length
        left = x[n // 2 - 1]      # element just left of centre
        right = x[n // 2]         # element just right of centre
        head = x[:n // 2 - 1]     # elements before the two centre ones
        tail = x[n // 2 + 1:]     # elements after the two centre ones

        if n == 4:                # the only even length where both sides have a single element
            # fill the four‑slot middle part with two copies of the outer element,
            # then the right centre, then the left centre
            middle = [head[0], head[0], right, left]
        elif left < right and n % 4 == 0:
            # when the left centre is smaller and the length is a multiple of 4,
            # mirror the two centre values
            middle = [right, left, left, right]
        else:
            # default case: right centre once, left centre three times
            middle = [right, left, left, left]

    return tail[::-1] + middle + head[::-1]

def transform(x):
    n = len(x)
    # odd length
    if n % 2 == 1:
        mid = x[n // 2]
        head = x[:n // 2]
        tail = x[n // 2 + 1:]
        # n ≡ 1 (mod 4) → use the element just before the centre twice
        if n % 4 == 1:
            middle = [head[-1], head[-1], mid]
        else:                     # n ≡ 3 (mod 4)
            middle = [mid, mid, mid]
        return tail[::-1] + middle + head[::-1]

    # even length
    # split around the two centre elements
    left = x[n // 2 - 1]          # element just left of centre
    right = x[n // 2]             # element just right of centre
    head = x[:n // 2 - 1]         # elements before the two centre ones
    tail = x[n // 2 + 1:]         # elements after the two centre ones

    # special handling for the smallest even size (n == 4)
    if n == 4:
        # head has exactly one element (the first one)
        middle = [head[0], head[0], right, left]
        return tail[::-1] + middle + head[::-1]

    # for larger even sizes
    if n % 4 == 0:                # length is a multiple of 4
        middle = [right, left, left, right]
    else:                         # length ≡ 2 (mod 4)
        middle = [right, left, left, left]

    return tail[::-1] + middle + head[::-1]

def transform(x):
    n = len(x)
    # odd length
    if n % 2 == 1:
        mid = x[n // 2]
        head = x[:n // 2]
        tail = x[n // 2 + 1:]
        # n ≡ 1 (mod 4) → use the element just before the centre twice
        if n % 4 == 1:
            middle = [head[-1], head[-1], mid]
        else:                     # n ≡ 3 (mod 4)
            middle = [mid, mid, mid]
        return tail[::-1] + middle + head[::-1]

    # even length
    # split around the two centre elements
    left = x[n // 2 - 1]          # element just left of centre
    right = x[n // 2]             # element just right of centre
    head = x[:n // 2 - 1]         # elements before the two centre ones
    tail = x[n // 2 + 1:]         # elements after the two centre ones

    # special handling for the smallest even size (n == 4)
    if n == 4:
        # head has exactly one element (the first one)
        middle = [head[0], head[0], right, left]
        return tail[::-1] + middle + head[::-1]

    # for larger even sizes
    if n % 4 == 0:                # length is a multiple of 4
        middle = [right, left, left, right]
    else:                         # length ≡ 2 (mod 4)
        middle = [right, left, left, left]

    return tail[::-1] + middle + head[::-1]

def transform(x):
    n = len(x)
    if n == 0:
        return []
    # even length
    if n % 2 == 0:
        left = x[:n // 2]
        right = x[n // 2:]
        rev_right = right[::-1]
        rev_left = left[::-1]

        if n % 4 == 0:                     # n ≡ 0 (mod 4)
            middle = [left[-1], left[-1], right[0]]
        else:                              # n ≡ 2 (mod 4)
            middle = [left[-1]] * 3

        # drop the first element of rev_left (the duplicated one)
        return rev_right + middle + rev_left[1:]

    # odd length
    else:
        left = x[:n // 2]
        mid = x[n // 2]
        right = x[n // 2 + 1:]
        rev_right = right[::-1]
        rev_left = left[::-1]

        if n % 4 == 3:                     # n ≡ 3 (mod 4)
            middle = [mid] * 3
        else:                              # n ≡ 1 (mod 4)
            # left is non‑empty for n≥3; for n==1 we just repeat the element
            if left:
                middle = [left[-1], left[-1], mid]
            else:
                middle = [mid] * 3

def transform(x):
    n = len(x)
    if n == 0:
        return []
    # even length
    if n % 2 == 0:
        left = x[:n // 2]
        right = x[n // 2:]
        rev_right = right[::-1]
        rev_left = left[::-1]

        if n % 4 == 0:                     # n ≡ 0 (mod 4)
            middle = [left[-1], left[-1], right[0]]
        else:                              # n ≡ 2 (mod 4)
            middle = [left[-1]] * 3

        # drop the first element of rev_left (the duplicated one)
        return rev_right + middle + rev_left[1:]

    # odd length
    else:
        left = x[:n // 2]
        mid = x[n // 2]
        right = x[n // 2 + 1:]
        rev_right = right[::-1]
        rev_left = left[::-1]

        if n % 4 == 3:                     # n ≡ 3 (mod 4)
            middle = [mid] * 3
        else:                              # n ≡ 1 (mod 4)
            # left is non‑empty for n≥3; for n==1 we just repeat the element
            if left:
                middle = [left[-1], left[-1], mid]
            else:
                middle = [mid] * 3

        return rev_right + middle + rev_left

def transform(x):
    n = len(x)
    if n == 0:
        return []

    # even length
    if n % 2 == 0:
        k = n // 2
        left = x[:k]
        right = x[k:]
        rev_right = right[::-1]
        rev_left = left[::-1]

        if n % 4 == 2:                     # n ≡ 2 (mod 4)
            middle = [left[-1]] * 3
            return rev_right + middle + rev_left[1:]

        # n ≡ 0 (mod 4)
        if n == 4:                         # the only even length where the rule differs
            # order: last of right, first of left (twice), first of right,
            # then the element of left that is farthest from the centre,
            # and finally the first of left again
            return [rev_right[0],
                    left[0], left[0],
                    right[0],
                    rev_left[0],
                    left[0]]
        else:
            middle = [left[-1], left[-1], right[0]]
            return rev_right + middle + rev_left[1:]

    # odd length
    else:
        k = n // 2
        left = x[:k]
        mid = x[k]
        right = x[k + 1:]
        rev_right = right[::-1]
        rev_left = left[::-1]

        if n % 4 == 3:                     # n ≡ 3 (mod 4)
            middle = [mid] * 3
        else:                              # n ≡ 1 (mod 4)
            if left:                       # n ≥ 3
                middle = [left[-1], left[-1], mid]
            else:                          # n == 1
                middle = [mid] * 3

        return rev_right + middle + rev_left

def transform(x):
    n = len(x)
    if n == 0:
        return []

    # even length
    if n % 2 == 0:
        k = n // 2
        left = x[:k]
        right = x[k:]
        rev_right = right[::-1]
        rev_left = left[::-1]

        if n % 4 == 2:                     # n ≡ 2 (mod 4)
            middle = [left[-1]] * 3
            return rev_right + middle + rev_left[1:]

        # n ≡ 0 (mod 4)
        if n == 4:                         # the only even length where the rule differs
            # order: last of right, first of left (twice), first of right,
            # then the element of left that is farthest from the centre,
            # and finally the first of left again
            return [rev_right[0],
                    left[0], left[0],
                    right[0],
                    rev_left[0],
                    left[0]]
        else:
            middle = [left[-1], left[-1], right[0]]
            return rev_right + middle + rev_left[1:]

    # odd length
    else:
        k = n // 2
        left = x[:k]
        mid = x[k]
        right = x[k + 1:]
        rev_right = right[::-1]
        rev_left = left[::-1]

        if n % 4 == 3:                     # n ≡ 3 (mod 4)
            middle = [mid] * 3
        else:                              # n ≡ 1 (mod 4)
            if left:                       # n ≥ 3
                middle = [left[-1], left[-1], mid]
            else:                          # n == 1
                middle = [mid] * 3

        return rev_right + middle + rev_left

def transform(x):
    n = len(x)
    if n == 0:
        return []

    # even length
    if n % 2 == 0:
        k = n // 2
        left = x[:k]
        right = x[k:]
        rev_right = right[::-1]
        rev_left = left[::-1]

        if n % 4 == 2:                     # n ≡ 2 (mod 4)
            middle = [left[-1]] * 3
            return rev_right + middle + rev_left[1:]

        # n ≡ 0 (mod 4)
        if n == 4:                         # the only even length where the rule differs
            # order: last of right, first of left (twice), first of right,
            # then the element of left that is farthest from the centre,
            # and finally the first of left again
            return [rev_right[0],
                    left[0], left[0],
                    right[0],
                    rev_left[0],
                    left[0]]
        else:
            middle = [left[-1], left[-1], right[0]]
            return rev_right + middle + rev_left[1:]

    # odd length
    else:
        k = n // 2
        left = x[:k]
        mid = x[k]
        right = x[k + 1:]
        rev_right = right[::-1]
        rev_left = left[::-1]

        if n % 4 == 3:                     # n ≡ 3 (mod 4)
            middle = [mid] * 3
        else:                              # n ≡ 1 (mod 4)
            if left:                       # n ≥ 3
                middle = [left[-1], left[-1], mid]
            else:                          # n == 1
                middle = [mid] * 3

        return rev_right + middle + rev_left

def transform(x):
    n = len(x)
    if n == 0:
        return []

    rev = x[::-1]

    # odd length → triple the middle element
    if n % 2 == 1:
        m = n // 2
        return rev[:m] + [rev[m]] * 3 + rev[m + 1:]

    # even length
    if n == 4:                     # special case for length‑4 lists
        first = x[0]
        return [rev[0]] + [first] * 2 + rev[1:3] + [first]

    k = n // 2                     # index of the right‑hand middle element in rev
    A = rev[k - 1]                 # left‑hand middle element
    B = rev[k]                     # right‑hand middle element

    if n % 4 == 0:                 # n ≡ 0 (mod 4) and n > 4
        # duplicate both middles once, order A B B A
        return rev[:k - 1] + [A, B, B, A] + rev[k + 1:]
    else:                          # n ≡ 2 (mod 4)

        return rev[:k - 1] + [A] + [B] * 3 + rev[k + 1:]
